id: Shaun Kirk (AUS)-The Petone Depot, Lower Hutt, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Shaun Kirk (AUS)
venue: The Petone Depot, Lower Hutt, Wellington
long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognized for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

id: Arturo Báez / Blair Latham Quartet-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Arturo Báez / Blair Latham Quartet
long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Arturo Báez / Blair Latham Quartet!

Arturo and Blair began their musical journey together when Blair moved to Mexico City in 2010 and became an integral part of the jazz and improv scenes. Both being in demand players, they were inevitably thrown together in many of the top creative projects that performed at the main jazz clubs of the day. Since Blair moved back to NZ in 2014 they have maintained a strong musical connection, and look forward to sharing their original compositions and improvisations –played with local legends Tyson Smith and Rick Cranson– with New Zealand audiences.

Arturo Báez is a Mexican double bassist and electric bassist whose music moves between jazz, free improvisation and spontaneous collective creation. For more than 15 years, he has been an active presence in Mexico's improvised music scene, collaborating with internationally acclaimed artists. His international work includes performances across the United States, Europe and Asia. He is a member of the Remi Álvarez Trio and leads Otrora un Simulacro, an original jazz ensemble that features his compositions.

Blair Latham is a saxophonist, composer and multi instrumentalist with a deep love of the bass clarinet. With a prodigious technique and an expansive creative vision –inspired by the likes of John Coltrane and Ornette Coleman– he can be found lending his talents to a diverse range of projects from Jazz to Pop to avant-garde around our capital city.

Thursday Nov 19
Doors 7pm
Music 7:30pm
$20

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆

name: Lily Atu Presents: Rivering
long_description:
Rivering at Rogue!

Come celebrate Rivering on the 19th of November with us. If you haven’t had a chance to catch us play yet, this gig is for you, and if you have already supported this project, come along, dance and grab a drink.

The collection of music entitled Rivering is written by saxophonist and vocalist Lily Rose Atu, and is deeply inspired by her love of jazz and neo-soul. It has been workshopped across the year with Jono Ben Zur (bass), Ranu Wijesuriya (drums), and Paulina Hernandez (piano) and has recently been recorded at Massey University.

Special features at this gig include Elisa Bird (clarinet and baritone) Frank Paton (trumpet) and Victoria Ferry (vocals). This will be our last gig with the incredible pianist Paulina who will be heading overseas just a few days after this show. Come and listen to the music we have created together for a final time!

Tickets from $10 at humanitix: https://events.humanitix.com/rivering-compositions-by-lily-rose-atu
Limited door sales: $15

name: Arturo Báez (mexico) Performance Residency - Night 1
long_description:
Pyramid Club is very happy to present the wonderful Mexican double bassist Arturo Báez for two nights, playing solo and in improvised collaborations with a host of top notch local musicians.


Arturo Báez Velázquez is a Mexican double bassist and electric bassist whose music moves between jazz, free improvisation and spontaneous collective creation. Báez was born in Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán. He began playing folkloric music of the region at the age of 14, and moved to Mexico City at 19 to pursue his musical studies.

For more than 15 years, he has been an active presence in Mexico’s improvised music scene, collaborating with internationally acclaimed artists including Ken Vandermark, Joe Morris, Chris Corsano, Michael Zerang, Sam Newsome, Isaiah Collier, Dennis Gonzalez, Blaise Siwula, Brian Allen, Leo Genovese, David Borgo, Linda Briceño, Justo Almario, Víctor Mendoza, Remi Álvarez, Cristóbal López, Héctor Infanzón, Gabriel Puentes and Alejandro Campos, among others.

A prolific artist, Arturo is a regular member of many projects including Big Band Jazz de México, the Remi Álvarez Trío, Chocolate Smoke Gang, Carlos Marx and the Jorge Fernández Project. His international work includes performances at the No Idea Festival in Austin and across the United States, Europe and Asia. He leads Otrora un Simulacro, a creative jazz ensemble that features his original compositions.

We’re also thrilled that Manda will be joining us for a few songs on the Persian daff, bringing the beautiful sounds of this traditional frame drum to the evening.

Join us for another evening of great music, dancing and good vibes. Tickets are koha – simply follow the link on Under the Radar or pay at the door.

We’d love to see you again!

id: Stretch to Mould-Nui Hui , Wainuiomata, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Stretch to Mould
long_description:
It's that magical time of the year where Nui Hui brings you a concert of phenomenal local talent.

Reggae, Rock, Soul, Metal, Pop, all under one roof here in good old Wainuiomata.

We've had an amazing line up of artist over the years and this year is no exception. Come join us for a musical spectacle not to be missed.

Stretch to Mould are a rock band from Wellington, New Zealand, formed in 2012 by vocalist and guitarist Darrell Vickers.

Known for their explosive live performances, hard-hitting riffs, powerful vocals, and uncompromising rock-and-roll attitude, the band have spent more than a decade refining their sound and building a loyal following.

Following the release of their debut album Shadows (2012) and the EP Painting Faces (2014), Stretch to Mould are entering a bold new chapter with their forthcoming album, Where Is the Moon?, due for release in 2027.

Bigger, louder, and more ambitious than anything the band has released before, the album showcases a significant leap forward in songwriting, production, musicianship, and sonic depth. Their recent single release Paper Mache is packed with memorable hooks, driving rhythms, and the band's most confident performance to date.
